task: t5 - video channel: real-encoded validation + inter-frame temporal evidence

declarations.brief_contains_no_video: TRUE. The OPEN-SZ-01 brief is 119 still images (data/images/*.png), zero videos. No probe/testset sample is a video.
declarations.channel_level_not_business_level: TRUE. Everything in this report is a CHANNEL-level result: it shows that a genuinely encoded video stream can be decoded, that per-frame evidence aggregates into a video verdict, and that the frozen stack stays inside the 5 s budget. It is NOT evidence of business-level video fraud-detection capability.
declarations.classes_are_separated_by_still_provenanc: TRUE. No AI-generated video and no real-shot video exist in this workspace. Both classes are still images turned into clips by the SAME deterministic synthetic motion + noise overlay; the only class difference is which still produced the frames.
declarations.clips_are_genuinely_encoded_not_copies: TRUE. Each clip has many distinct decoded frames (see per-clip decoded_distinct_frames) and the codec performs real inter-frame prediction; no clip is one still written N times.
declarations.no_threshold_weight_or_feature_was_fitte: TRUE. Thresholds come from the a-priori fp-budget rule; the temporal features are fixed formulas from src/video_temporal.py; no classifier was trained.
declarations.gap_vs_real_video: OPEN. Substituting real-shot and AI-generated video (see data_sources) is still required before any capability claim; the motion/noise overlay is a synthesis, not camera physics, and the real class of arm A is web-sourced re-encoded JPEGs rather than a real capture pipeline.

environment.encoder: cv2.VideoWriter (OpenCV-built encoder; ffmpeg CLI not required)

protocol.preregistered_note: Every value below was fixed before the first clip was encoded and before any score existed. No threshold, weight, feature or generator was selected on the evaluated clips; the video-level decision threshold is the a-priori rule 'allow exactly fp_budget false positives among the arm's real clips'.

arms.A_source_controlled: real = repo/testset/real real claim photos (web-sourced, re-encoded JPEG); fake = data/images AI stills
arms.B_in_domain_same_source: real = data/images real stills (seq 57+); fake = the SAME AI clips as arm A - replicates the archived 30-clip protocol with more clips

protocol.video_path: production detector.detect_video: 10-frame uniform sampling -> per-frame CLIP/forensic evidence -> 0.5*mean + 0.5*P90
protocol.temporal_feature_input: ALL decoded frames of the clip (24), not the 10 sampled ones

identical_across_classes: motion field (sub-pixel sinusoidal pan + slow zoom)
per-frame noise realisation (seeded by frame index only)
construction.arm_A_real: repo/testset/real/*.jpg - web-sourced genuine claim photographs (index: repo/testset/real/_real_claim_index.json); JPEG from a CDN, re-encoded, no EXIF
construction.arm_A_fake: data/images AI stills (seq 1..), labels from data/labels.csv
construction.arm_B_real: data/images real stills (seq 57+) - the brief's own in-domain real class
construction.arm_B_fake: the SAME clips as arm A fake (shared, scored once)
construction.known_confound_arm_A: repo/reports/testset_real_41_eval.md measured the frozen image heads at FPR 92.7% on these very web-sourced real photos (OOD vs the brief's real cluster). Arm A therefore mixes 'video channel behaviour' with a KNOWN image-head domain gap and must not be read as a video-only statement.

validation_set.selection_rule: frozen sorted-order prefix, see build_manifest docstring

checks.description: re-computing the same frames yields bit-identical values
two different still images yield different (not just re-scaled) feature values
every feature is finite (no NaN/inf) on a real sequence
an all-identical frame list gives ~zero flow
repeated frames give residual correlation ~1 (documents what the continuity feature measures)
the synthesised pan/zoom produces non-zero flow
fewer than MIN_FRAMES frames raise instead of returning junk

video_level.note: video-level metrics of the t5 controlled set; arm A is the task-required source-controlled arm, arm B replicates the archived in-domain protocol. Channel-level, NOT business-level.
video_level.interpretation: PRIMARY arm = A_source_controlled, as required by the task (real = repo/testset/real claim photos, fake = data/images AI stills). It must be read together with validation_set.construction.known_confound_arm_A: the frozen image heads score those web-sourced real photos as AI at 92.7% FPR (repo/reports/testset_real_41_eval.md), so a low arm-A AUC reflects that known image-domain gap, not the temporal features. Arm B (B_in_domain_same_source, both classes from the brief) is the arm to compare with the archived 30-clip run.

latency_ms.measured_on: all clips, wall clock around detect_video()

latency_ms_excluding_cold_start.measured_on: 59 clips, first (cold-start) clip excluded; the excluded clip carries the one-time model load exactly as in the archived run

temporal_features.interpretation: The two arms receive an IDENTICAL synthetic motion field and IDENTICAL per-frame noise realisation, so any temporal difference only reflects how the still's content interacts with motion + noise + codec. A near-0.5 AUC here is an honest negative result for these features on this set, not a bug; a high AUC would still not establish AI-video detection, because neither class is real video.

label_free_composite.definition: mean of z-scored AI-like-oriented temporal features (z computed over all evaluated clips; NO labels used)
label_free_composite.note: exploratory only: it is a fixed unweighted average, not a trained model, and it was not used to select anything

archived_protocol.video_path: 10-frame uniform sampling -> per-frame forensic+global-CLIP evidence -> mean/P90 aggregation (production path)

comparison_to_archived_30_clips.archived_synthesis: archived clips were built with a global brightness ramp (1+0.02t-0.01) on one still - i.e. no real inter-frame motion; the t5 clips add a sub-pixel pan/zoom + per-frame noise, so they exercise the codec's inter-frame prediction

t5_latency_ms_all_clips.measured_on: all clips, wall clock around detect_video()

comparison_to_archived_30_clips.same_protocol_note: Both runs use the identical production video path (10-frame uniform sampling -> per-frame evidence -> 0.5*mean + 0.5*P90 aggregation), the identical frozen fusion config and the identical video-level metric definitions (AUC + fp-budget threshold). The differences are clip synthesis, clip count and the real-class source.

detector_config_note: same PipelineConfig as scripts/video_channel_validation.py (root models/ dir, clip_probe_norm.pt, root fusion.json) so the archived 30-clip numbers are directly comparable

data_sources.status: NOT ACQUIRED - nothing below is present in the workspace; this is the input list for the next step
data_sources.why_this_section_exists: F1-F7 in the t1 baseline showed the headline numbers depend on corpora that are missing from the repo. Video must not repeat that: the acquisition list is written down before any video metric is quoted.
real_shot_collection_requirements: Device/params: native camera app (no in-app sharing), >=1080p, 30fps, H.264/H.265, >=3s and <=15s per clip, auto-exposure locked where possible; the ORIGINAL file must be transferred by cable/cloud-upload, never re-sent through WeChat/Douyin (their re-encode destroys the very noise/frequency statistics this channel measures).

Metadata: keep EXIF/QuickTime atoms (device model, ISO, exposure, capture time, GPS with PII masking); record a per-file sha256 plus capture sheet (device, fps, duration, scene, lighting, operator, consent id).

Scene coverage: the four claim families the business actually sees - vehicle collision/damage, property water/fire damage, damaged goods, injury/medical-bill handheld capture. At least 2 devices and 2 lighting conditions per family.

Paired design: for every real scenario also record a same-scenario AI/synthesised clip, and log generator name+version, prompt, seed and duration for each fake; >=5 distinct generators so the result is not one-model-specific.
Volume: >=200 real and >=200 AI clips is the minimum for a video-level 2-FP budget to be meaningful (with 20 real clips one FP step is 5 percentage points).
Hard negatives: blurry/old footage, footage of a screen (翻拍), and genuinely real clips that were cropped/filtered afterwards - labelling all of those as AI would inflate the score.
Compliance: written usage authorisation, PII redaction, no re-distribution outside the evaluation pool, and a licence field per clip.

data_sources.minimum_next_step: Download one real+AI video pair corpus with a matching real class (GenVideo/DeMamba or DFDC for a start), re-run this exact script with real clips substituted for the encoded stills, and report the video-level metrics under the same frozen protocol.

headline.what_this_establishes: A genuinely encoded video stream (24 distinct frames per clip, real codec inter-frame prediction) is decoded, scored end-to-end by the production video path, aggregated into a video verdict, and stays inside the 5 s budget on this machine - plus an inter-frame temporal feature block that is unit-tested.
headline.what_this_does_NOT_establish: Any business-level real-vs-AI VIDEO detection capability. The brief contains no video; both classes are stills turned into clips; no real-shot and no AI-generated video was available offline.
